evals.prompt:
Write specs for a User model. The model has `has_many :posts`, `has_many :comments`, a `#full_name` method that combines first_name and last_name, and a `#deactivate!` method that sets `active: false` and cancels all pending posts. Use FactoryBot. Here are the relevant model files:

```ruby
# app/models/user.rb
class User < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :posts, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy

  validates :first_name, :last_name, :email, presence: true
  validates :email, uniqueness: true

  def full_name
    "#{first_name} #{last_name}"
  end

  def deactivate!
    transaction do
      update!(active: false)
      posts.pending.find_each(&:cancel!)
    end
  end
end
```

```ruby
# app/models/post.rb
class Post < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :user
  belongs_to :category, optional: true

  enum :status, { draft: 0, pending: 1, published: 2, cancelled: 3 }

  def cancel!
    update!(status: :cancelled, cancelled_at: Time.current)
  end
end
```
evals.expected_output: A well-structured RSpec file using let_it_be, build_stubbed where appropriate, and create_default for associations
expectations: Uses let_it_be for shared records instead of let!
Uses build_stubbed or build (not create) for #full_name test since no DB is needed
Tests #deactivate! verifies both active: false AND pending posts cancelled
Does not use message expectations (expect().to receive) to test implementation details
Multiple related assertions grouped in same example rather than split into one-assertion-per-test

evals.prompt:
These tests are really slow, can you help me speed them up?

```ruby
# spec/models/board_spec.rb
RSpec.describe Board do
  describe '#add_member' do
    let!(:account) { create(:account) }
    let!(:owner) { create(:user, account: account) }
    let!(:board) { create(:board, owner: owner, account: account) }
    let!(:new_member) { create(:user, account: account) }

    it 'adds the user as a member' do
      board.add_member(new_member)
      expect(board.members).to include(new_member)
    end

    it 'sets the default role to viewer' do
      membership = board.add_member(new_member)
      expect(membership.role).to eq('viewer')
    end

    it 'does not add duplicate members' do
      board.add_member(new_member)
      board.add_member(new_member)
      expect(board.memberships.where(user: new_member).count).to eq(1)
    end
  end

  describe '#archive' do
    let!(:account) { create(:account) }
    let!(:owner) { create(:user, account: account) }
    let!(:board) { create(:board, owner: owner, account: account) }
    let!(:column1) { create(:column, board: board) }
    let!(:column2) { create(:column, board: board) }
    let!(:card1) { create(:card, column: column1, creator: owner) }
    let!(:card2) { create(:card, column: column1, creator: owner) }
    let!(:card3) { create(:card, column: column2, creator: owner) }

    it 'marks the board as archived' do
      board.archive
      expect(board.archived?).to be true
    end

    it 'archives all cards' do
      board.archive
      expect(board.cards.reload).to all(be_archived)
    end

    it 'records the archived_at timestamp' do
      freeze_time do
        board.archive
        expect(board.archived_at).to eq(Time.current)
      end
    end

    it 'is idempotent' do
      board.archive
      expect { board.archive }.not_to raise_error
    end
  end
end
```

expectations: Converts let! to let_it_be for shared records
Uses create_default to eliminate duplicate account/owner creation across describe blocks
Uses before_all or let_it_be for the heavy archive setup (columns + cards)
Includes explanation of what changed and why
Uses appropriate let_it_be modifiers (reload/refind) for records that get mutated

evals.prompt:
Add specs for this Card::Closeable concern. Closing creates a Closure record with the user who closed it, reopening destroys the closure. A card that's already closed can't be closed again.

```ruby
# app/models/card/closeable.rb
module Card::Closeable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_one :closure, dependent: :destroy
  end

  def closed?
    closure.present?
  end

  def close(user: Current.user)
    return if closed?

    transaction do
      create_closure!(user: user)
      track_event(:closed, creator: user)
    end
  end

  def reopen(user: Current.user)
    return unless closed?

    transaction do
      closure.destroy!
      track_event(:reopened, creator: user)
    end
  end
end
```

```ruby
# app/models/closure.rb
class Closure < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :card
  belongs_to :user
end
```
evals.expected_output: Specs for the concern using let_it_be, testing behavior not implementation, with proper TestProf patterns
expectations: Uses let_it_be for card and user setup records
Has examples covering all three methods: #close, #reopen, and #closed?
Covers edge cases: closing already-closed card and reopening already-open card
Does not use message expectations (expect().to receive) to test implementation details
Uses let_it_be modifiers (reload/refind) appropriately for records that get mutated by tests
